@RepMGP There is no Hospital in Skamania. However $50 billion was in the fund to support rural hospitals. The Rural Health Transformation Program, is intended to mitigate the impact of Medicaid cuts on  hospitals.

Rural hospital closures are a symptom of systemic failure, not just funding gaps. The real issue? Bloated bureaucracies and misplaced priorities. While Medicaid expansion strains rural hospitals with low reimbursement rates, the $53 million cut is a drop in the bucket compared to the $29.5 billion Washington spent on ambulatory care in 2022 alone. Studies show closures haven’t notably worsened health outcomes—because patients adapt by seeking higher-quality care elsewhere.

But this exposes the rot: hospitals charging $100 facility fees per visit while operating at 83% Medicare payment-to-cost ratios scream inefficiency. Instead of throwing taxpayer cash at broken models, we need price transparency, anti-consolidation measures, and redirecting funds from administrative bloat to frontline care.

Foreign aid and bureaucratic pet projects shouldn’t drain resources while rural Americans foot the bill for DC’s incompetence.
@RepMGP What is YOUR solution for fixing the problem? Throw more money into a broken system?

Rural hospitals are crumbling under bureaucratic bloat and unchecked abuse. The Distressed Hospital Grant program proves Washington’s priorities are backwards—patching leaks instead of fixing the dam. Medicaid’s collapse isn’t just about funding cuts; it’s structural theft. Every dollar wasted on inefficiency or illegal immigration is stolen from citizens who paid in.

Real reform means slashing red tape, enforcing borders, and redirecting funds to frontline care—not propping up a broken system. Emergency costs spike when D.C. refuses to address the root causes: open-door policies and a refusal to prioritize Americans.

Secure the system, secure the border, then watch rural health thrive.
